headline: Mythos 5.5 looms over Anthropic's IPO countdown; OpenAI's raise shrinks; agents get their own git forge
tldr: Anthropic looks days away from launching Claude Mythos 5.5 as its IPO roadshow approaches. OpenAI revised its raise down to $20B at a $1.25T valuation with about $11B secured so far. And the dev-tool stack keeps re-forming around agents: an ex-GitHub CEO launched an agent-first git forge, while hiring data names agentic AI the fastest-growing skill in job descriptions.

stories.title: Claude Mythos 5.5 reference appears on Anthropic's site — launch may be days away
stories.summary: A 'Claude Mythos 5.5' mention was spotted on Anthropic's official Mythos webpage — a recent addition, absent from the October 23 snapshot. Mythos is Anthropic's model class for cybersecurity and biology research; Mythos 5.1 was restricted to verified researchers while Fable 5.1 offered the same underlying model with added safeguards for general use. The timing lands just as Anthropic — which filed its S-1 on October 26 under ticker ANT — is expected to start its IPO roadshow later this month.
stories.why_it_matters: A new Claude model class plus Anthropic's trusted-access pattern is directly relevant to CCAR-P's Models and Governance domains — and to how you pick models for client work.

stories.title: DeepSeek's Super-Agent goes open-source: Router + Worker architecture for autonomous coding
stories.summary: DeepSeek's Harness team released an open-source prototype of 'Super-Agent,' an autonomous coding agent that monitors developer group chats and GitHub, identifies bugs, and can reproduce them and open a pull request without being tagged or prompted. The design splits the system into a Router layer that holds broader context and parallel Worker sessions that execute coding tasks. The launch is timed against Anthropic's expected IPO roadshow.
stories.why_it_matters: A direct shot at Claude Code — the tool you build with daily — and the Router/Worker pattern is a concrete agent architecture to study for your Life Time follow-up agent.

stories.title: OpenAI cuts its raise to $20B at a $1.25T valuation; about $11B secured
stories.summary: OpenAI revised its funding target down from $30B to $20B at a $1.25T post-money valuation (down from $1.4T), per CNBC and FT reporting. The WSJ reports about $11B is secured so far, with UAE investors (including state-backed MGX) and Coatue leading and Founders Fund, Sequoia and a16z expected to participate; the round remains open. Reporting links the smaller target to investor caution over AI infrastructure spending and a tech selloff — and to Anthropic's IPO competing for the same capital.
stories.why_it_matters: Follow-up to Saturday's item. Even the top of the market is repricing — useful macro context for your March 2027 job-hunt timing and contracting rates.

stories.title: Ex-GitHub CEO launches Entire, an agent-first git forge; Infisical raises $40M for an Agent Vault
stories.summary: Thomas Dohmke (former GitHub CEO) publicly launched Entire, a git forge built for coding agents: pull requests are replaced by 'Trails' (agent-scored evals), a codebase graph cuts token usage, and a Continuous Memory layer keeps context across multi-agent sessions. Separately, Infisical announced a $40M Series B at a reported $600M valuation to expand secrets and privileged-access tooling, including an 'Agent Vault' that lets agents reach systems without exposing raw keys.
stories.why_it_matters: The dev stack is being rebuilt for agent swarms — the infrastructure under your Cursor/Claude workflow is shifting, and FDE roles will expect fluency here.

stories.title: Agentic AI is the fastest-growing skill in job descriptions, says WTW
stories.summary: WTW's Q3 2026 Talent Intelligence Report — based on hiring at 1,500+ organisations in H1 2026 — found agentic AI the fastest-growing skill in job descriptions globally (and in North America), with AI governance third globally and second in Europe. Demand for AI engineers was strongest in software products, consulting and pharma; customer service reps, software engineers and account managers were the most in-demand roles overall.
stories.why_it_matters: Employers are literally writing agentic AI and AI governance into job descriptions — the same 35% of the CCAR-P that has no Foundations counterpart. Your exam-first bet matches the hiring data.

stories.title: Microsoft details the trojanized Claude-branded VS Code extension that hit the Cursor marketplace
stories.summary: Microsoft Security Research published a technical analysis of the trojanized Claude-branded VS Code extension briefly distributed through the Cursor marketplace: it attempted to plant a persistent SSH backdoor. Cursor removed the malicious build and published remediation guidance. The incident is a reminder that agent tooling and SDK supply chains are a direct attack surface.
stories.why_it_matters: Follow-up to Friday's Cursor story. Check your own extensions' publisher provenance — your dev machine is the supply chain.

for_davis: Exam-first read: Mythos/Fable model classes and trusted-access patterns sit in CCAR-P Models territory, and WTW's hiring data puts agentic AI plus AI governance — the 35% of your exam with no Foundations counterpart — at the top of what employers now write into job descriptions. The Super-Agent and Entire launches are agent-architecture case studies worth ten minutes for your Life Time build.
